about.title: Temple City Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Temple City's economy runs on a mix of small retail, warehousing, and service businesses tucked along corridors like Temple City Boulevard and Lower Azusa Road, and workers moving between job sites face real risk from forklifts, delivery vehicles, and understaffed crews. When an injury happens on the clock, California generally routes the claim through workers' compensation regardless of fault, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party injury claim may be possible alongside comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement — we simply listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can explain your specific situation, including deadlines and whether a third-party claim applies. There's no cost to talk it through, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Temple City Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Spot Third-Party Claims
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent contractor, property owner, or equipment maker can still be liable. We connect you with an attorney who can evaluate whether a separate claim applies to your accident.

items.title: We Know the 30-Day Reporting Window Matters
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report to their employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. An attorney in our network can help you understand where you stand and what to do next.

items.title: Retaliation Concerns Are Taken Seriously
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If that's happened, the attorney we connect you with can walk through what protections may apply to your case.

items.question: I was hurt at a warehouse job near Rosemead Boulevard — can I still sue my employer?
items.answer: In most cases, workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, so a direct lawsuit against them is usually not available. However, if a third party like a subcontractor, delivery company, or equipment manufacturer contributed to your injury, a separate claim against them may be possible. An attorney can review the specifics of your accident to see what applies.

items.question: Does it matter that my accident happened in Temple City specifically?
items.answer: California's workers' comp and third-party liability rules apply statewide, so the core legal framework is the same everywhere. That said, local factors — like which businesses operate along corridors such as Las Tunas Drive or Temple City Boulevard, and who owns or maintains those job sites — can affect who might be a liable third party. An independent attorney familiar with these details can help sort that out.

items.question: What if I already reported my injury late?
items.answer: California generally asks injured workers to report within 30 days, and missing that deadline can create complications but doesn't automatically end your options. It's worth discussing the specifics with an attorney rather than assuming the claim is closed. There's no cost to have that conversation through LawProactive.
